attributes.residual: SCHEDULE + volatile-FPR colouring, ONE named window. Structure: opcode multiset IDENTICAL 138/138, frame 0x1C0 exact, _savefpr_28 exact, all 12 quad stores and both NormalVector calls exact. The whole residual is (a) a volatile-FPR renaming that starts at the very first instruction after the prologue - target loads the first f64 constant into f2 and gClockTime into f0, ours loads them into f0 and f1, and that single choice propagates a 4-register rotation through the entire entry block even though the instruction ORDER there is byte-for-byte identical - and (b) one 28-instruction reorder window at 0x150-0x1bc where target interleaves quad[0]/quad[1]/quad[2] between the p0 and p1 fmadds while ours emits all six p0/p1 values first. Consequence of (b): target colours w[0]/w[1] into the NV pair f29/f28 (short p1 live ranges) where ours colours p1x/p1y there (long live ranges). NOT WEBFRANK-READY: the discriminant in claim.law.webfrank-permutation-is-audited-in-our-colouring fails - this is not a pure instruction permutation (it is a permutation PLUS a register rotation, and permute_instruction_atoms runs its dependence audit on OUR pre-recolour image, where target's interleaving of quad[0] between p0x and p0y is only legal under target's f29/f28 assignment, not ours). Do not flag it.
